start.summary:
I built start.html as one continuous prototype from a copy of browse-c. browse-c.html and game-classic.html are unchanged.

What the player sees, step by step:
- **Steps 1 to 3.** These are browse-c as it was: the same cards, the same small pass with Area, Platform and Deck, the same travelling names and the same back motion.
- **Choosing a deck.** There is no sheet any more. The pass reflows in one beat of about 360 ms: the deck code flies from its card into the first column, and Cloud and AWS shrink up into one quiet line ("Cloud · AWS"). The fields underneath become Deck, Section and Class. The top zone stays 176 px tall, so the card list below never moves.
- **Why the quiet line.** I chose it over four columns because each value keeps a readable width. Five columns would have squeezed "Whole deck" and "Three lives" down to ellipses. It also previews the route shape (deck, then section) that the game ticket uses.
- **Step 4, Section.** Same plain cards as the deck step: "Whole deck" first (All 4 sections, 214 cards), then CON, SEC, TEC and BIL with code, name and card count. All five fit without scrolling.
- **CDL.** Cloud Digital Leader skips step 4 and writes "Whole deck" into the Section field. Back from Class then returns to the deck step.
- **Step 5, "Choose how to play".** Classic, Streak, Three lives and Timed as the same cards. The stub shows "Best" with 9 / of 10, 12 / in a row, 21 / cards, and "– / not yet" for Timed. Bests only exist for the CLF to SEC route; every other route shows "not yet".
- **After a class is chosen.** The pass grows in place into the game's ticket head: a 44 px band with the cloud icon and BOARDING PASS, CLF → SEC legs with names, and Class / Best / Gate. It sits at y = 120, exactly where the game ticket sits. Below it is "Your pass is ready", one muted sentence (the mode description plus "Swipe right for true, left for false.") and the "Start round" button, placed exactly where the False / True buttons will be.
- **Start round.** The same paper unrolls downward into the full first card: the statement "In the shared responsibility model, AWS is responsible for security of the cloud.", the perforation, and the stub with route, barcode and hint. Back turns into the close button and the 1-of-10 flight path, "Best 9 / 10" becomes "Card 01 / 10", and Start round becomes False / True. Close rolls it back up.
- **Returning player.** Step 1 adds one quiet row at the very bottom: "Continue where you left off", with "CLF → SEC · Classic · last 7 of 10" under it. Tapping it goes straight to the completed pass with Start round (see open questions). Its screen-reader label gives the full names.
- **First run.** Set `data-player="new"` on the root, or open the file with `#first-run`, to see step 1 without the continue row.
- **Back and field taps.** Back works at every step and reverses the motion. Tapping a filled field jumps back to its step: Cloud and AWS on the quiet line, Deck, Section, Class, or the CLF / SEC legs and the Class cell on the finished pass. Every choice from that step on is cleared, the value flies back to its card, and the others fade out.
- **data-demo** is on the Cloud, AWS, CLF and CLF's Security and compliance cards, in that order.

How I checked it:
- The screenshot tool reported "ok (5 shots)" with no errors and no horizontal overflow.
- My own Playwright script (`start-check.mjs`) saved start-6.png (class chosen) and start-7.png (after Start). It also confirmed the jumps (Deck tap to step 3, Area tap to step 1, Continue to the ready step, right leg to step 4), the CDL skip and its double back to step 3, first run, and reduced motion. No console errors.
- I took mid-transition frames at 100, 150 and 250 ms for every forward and back step.

What the frames caught, and the fixes:
- **First pass:** during the reflow, two names overlapped as they crossfaded ("Clas" over "sic"), because the opacity swap was riding the eased clock. I moved the fade onto its own linear clock, so the two looks swap halfway along.
- **Second pass:** the stub's paper turned see-through mid-grow, and when closing the round, the step-6 text showed through the paper as it rolled up. Now only the print fades and the paper itself stays solid, and the step-6 text waits until the paper has rolled up past it.
- **Smaller fixes:** the continue line was cut off; "not played" spilled out of its stub (now "not yet"); and the ready sentence repeated the best score already shown on the pass.

The final frames show no jumps.
start.openQuestions:
1. Continue lands on the completed pass with "Start round" (two taps to play), not straight into the round. My reason: the player sees the route and can still change the class before playing. If the client means one tap all the way into play, it is a single line to change: `go(7)` instead of `go(6)` in the #cont handler.
2. On the finished pass the middle meta cell reads "Best 9 / 10" and becomes "Card 01 / 10" at Start. With no best yet it reads "None".
3. The "Whole deck" route shows the code ALL on the ticket's right leg, as browse-c's sheet did, with "Whole deck" underneath.
4. The first statements for routes other than CLF to SEC are placeholders I wrote. They should be checked against the real deck content.
5. False / True on the started card do nothing, as allowed by the brief.
start.shotCheck: The screenshot tool printed "ok (5 shots)": start-1 is step 1 for a returning player, start-2 the platform step, start-3 the deck step, start-4 the section step on the route pass, and start-5 the class step with bests. My own script (Playwright, Chrome, 390x844) saved start-6 (Classic chosen: the completed boarding pass at y=120 and Start round) and start-7 (after Start: the full game ticket with the first statement, flight path at card 1 of 10, False / True). I read all seven, and start-7 matches game-classic's layout pixel for pixel in position. Mid-transition frames at 100, 150 and 250 ms for every forward step, every back step, the field jumps and Continue are in the scratchpad's `start/` folder. Two rounds of fixes (overlapping crossfade, see-through paper, text overlap when closing the round) left no jumps in the final frames. No console errors and no horizontal overflow.

night.summary:
I made start-night.html as a copy of start.html. Its :root is the night block from game-classic-night.html, copied as is: sky, surfaces, inks, accents, --on-accent, --cloud and the four shadow tokens, including --shadow-sm, --shadow-btn and --shadow-press. Behaviour, data, the motion code and the data-demo attributes are all unchanged. The title is now "Truthy: Start a round, night". start.html is not modified.

Colours that were hard-coded in start.html, now moved into tokens:
1. .soft box-shadow (back button, pass, close button, cards): rgba(16,35,63,…) became var(--shadow-sm).
2. .btn box-shadow became var(--shadow-btn), and .btn:active became var(--shadow-press).
3. The pressed tint rgba(16,35,63,.05) on .hit, .lv, .leg and .cont is now var(--press). This is one new token. The old dark tint could not be seen on the night paper.

Components that did not work with the night tokens, each fixed with the smallest change:
1. Text and icons on the amber band used var(--ink). At night that is light off-white on amber, so contrast was too low. These now use var(--on-accent) (7.79:1 on the amber): the .p-car band text, the small pass icon (.ico-s), the big pass cloud (.ico-b), the strokes of the step-1 logo, the logo in the continue row, and the plane on the round's flight path. I added two helper classes for this, .f-on-acc and .s-on-acc, which are the same ones game-classic-night uses.
2. The big pass cloud was missed in my first pass and showed light on the amber band in step 7. I fixed it and re-shot.

Contrast checked with the night values: --ink-muted on paper 5.35, on the sunk surface 6.04, on the sky bands 6.09 to 7.25. --ink on paper 10.48. --false and --true text on paper 4.94 and 4.72. Dark text on the light Start round button 13.59, and on the True and False buttons 6.12 and 6.40. All are 4.5:1 or above.

Decorative lines and dashes (--rule on paper) measure 1.43:1, against 1.47:1 in day, so the look is the same. The disabled cards (DevOps, Azure) measure 1.03:1 against their sky band, against 1.06:1 in day. They stay a quiet, flat placeholder, and their text reads at 6:1. I left both alone.

The light Start round pill matches the approved Next card button in game-classic-night, so it is not a new glaring surface.
night.newTokens: --press: rgba(230,227,218,.06). It is the pressed tint on pass fields, the area/platform line, the ticket legs and the continue row; the day value is rgba(16,35,63,.05). All other tokens (--on-accent, --shadow-sm, --shadow-btn, --shadow-press) come word for word from the game-classic-night block.
night.openQuestions:
1. start.html (day) still has the four rgba colours hard-coded. If the day file is meant to share the token set, the colleague could add --shadow-sm, --shadow-btn, --shadow-press, --press and --on-accent (day value var(--ink)) and use the same .f-on-acc and .s-on-acc helpers. Then the night file would truly differ only in :root.
2. The dot between "Cloud · AWS" on the pass is --rule colour and barely visible in both themes (1.4:1). It is decorative and hidden from screen readers. Making it --ink-muted would be a design call for both themes, not a night fix, so I left it.
night.shotCheck:
shot2.mjs printed "ok (5 shots)" and wrote start-night-1 to -5: area (returning player), platform, deck, section and class. A second script, start-night-check.mjs in the scratchpad, captured step 6 (pass ready) and step 7 (first card) as start-night-6 and -7. It also captured, in the scratchpad startnight/ folder, mid-transition frames for every forward step, keyboard focus, a pressed pass field, the #first-run view and the CDL path that skips the section step. It reported no page errors.

I read every PNG, with game-classic-night-1 and -2 open next to them. Step 7 now matches the night game screen: the same dark cloud and plane on the amber band, the same paper, the same muted labels, a light barcode and the same lifted True and False colours. Steps 1 to 6 have the same calm: dim slate cards on the deepening sky, warm off-white type and no glare. The focus ring (off-white, 3px) is clearly visible, and the pressed tint can be seen without shouting.

states.summary:
I built five new state screens, each copied from the screen it belongs to, with only what the state needs changed. I didn't touch any existing file.

1. game-timed-up (from game-timed): the clock reads 0:00 and the plane sits on the destination, with all quarter marks passed. The labels show 14 correct and 3 wrong, matching result-timed's 17 cards. Card 18 stays on the pass but can't be answered: the statement is muted, the Gate field reads "Closed", there's no swipe, and the True/False row is gone. An ink-coloured "Time is up" stamp with a clock glyph lands on the barcode, using the same animation as the Correct stamp in Timed. Below it a line reads "This card doesn't count · 17 answered", and the only action is a dark "See results →" button. There are no alarm colours and no shaking.

2. game-streak-record (from game-streak): card 13, with streak 12 and best 12. The flight path is now drawn by a script and works for any streak at or past the best:
   - It has one waypoint per card and rescales so the card in play sits near the end.
   - The old best keeps a ring on card 12, and the route runs on into open dotted sky with no destination circle.
   - Past waypoints shrink to plain dots for long streaks. I checked a 31-card streak in a scratch copy and the path doesn't crowd.

   Answering False (data-demo is on it) turns waypoint 13 into a green check and changes the labels to "Streak 13" and "Previous best 12". In the slip, a green "New best" stamp with a star replaces "Correct", in the same style as result-timed, with the word "Correct" kept for screen readers. That stamp is the only celebration on the screen.

3. game-lives-out (from game-lives): card 21, 1 of 3 lives left, 20 answered, with wrong marks on cards 6 and 15. Answering True (data-demo moved there) shows:
   - The last heart is drawn as a struck-through outline, so the loss is shown by shape, not colour, with a short slash animation as the stamp lands.
   - The label reads "No lives left" and the count reads 21 answered.
   - The trail gets its third wrong mark, and the "Not quite" stamp and the card's explanation stay visible.
   - The action becomes "See results →".

4. result-streak: "Correct in a row 13" with the "New best" stamp and "Previous best 12" under it. The path shows 13 checks, a ring on card 12 and a wrong mark on card 14. The header reads "Ended · 14 cards" and "13 correct · 1 wrong". One missed card is listed: card 14, the security awareness training card.

5. result-lives: "Cards answered 21" with "Equals your best / Best 21 cards", and no stamp, because equalling isn't a new best. The pass fields show Three lives, Correct 18 and Missed 03, the path has 21 waypoints, and the header reads "Out of lives" and "18 correct · 3 wrong". Three missed cards are listed: 06, 15 and 21.

Card content: card 06 (security awareness training) and card 21 (IAM role permissions policy) are reused, explanations included, from result-classic. Card 15 is the guest OS patching card, using the explanation from the game screens. This follows the trail in the approved game-lives screen, where card 6 was already wrong and a wrong answer on card 15 costs the second life.
states.newTokens: none. The new screens use only colours from the reference :root.
states.openQuestions:
1. Route mismatch: game-timed is CLF → SEC, but the approved result-timed is CLF → ALL. I kept SEC on game-timed-up because it copies game-timed. One of the two approved screens needs to change so the time-up and result screens show the same route.
2. Card 15 in result-lives: the brief asked me to reuse missed cards from result-classic and result-timed only. I used the guest OS patching card (with its explanation from the game screens) because the other reusable cards (Auto Scaling, VPC subnet, EBS, Budgets) aren't security cards and would look wrong in a CLF → SEC round. If strict reuse matters more, card 15 can swap to one of those.
3. Should the time-up state move keyboard focus? I left focus where it is, because focusing "See results" on load put a bright focus ring in the screenshot. A comment in the file says that in the app, focus should move to "See results" when the clock hits 0:00 while a True or False button has keyboard focus.
4. result-streak has only one missed card, so the lower part of the pass is mostly empty. Showing that card's explanation open by default would fill it, but I kept it collapsed (with data-demo on Why) to match the other result screens.
states.shotCheck:
All five screens passed the screenshot tool with "ok" (no console errors, no horizontal overflow). I read every PNG next to its source screen's shot: game-timed-up-1, game-streak-record-1 and -2, game-lives-out-1 and -2, result-streak-1 and -2, result-lives-1 and -2. Paper, type, density and stamp language all match, with no new colours. Fixes made between rounds:
- On both result screens the route labels were running into each other; I shortened them to "Ended · 14 cards" and "Out of lives".
- On result-streak the New best stamp was pressing against the ticket edge; "in a row" moved into the field label above the 13.
- On result-lives the 21 waypoints were crowded; I reduced them to radius 4.6.
- On game-timed-up the "Not counted" line was unclear and became "This card doesn't count · 17 answered".

One small leftover: in the streak-record question state the plane overlaps the best ring on card 12 by about 2px. It reads fine, but it's there.

system.tokenCounts:

- 146 aliases, none broken.
- Only valid DTCG types: color, dimension, fontFamily, fontWeight, duration, cubicBezier, number, typography, shadow, transition.
- Day and night define the same colour roles and the same elevation recipes.

opacity.pill-hint (0.75) is defined in the reference CSS but used by no screen, so it is marked "unused".
system.disagreements:
Rule applied: where the reference sets a value, the reference wins. Where it sets none, both values are kept and documented.

| Topic | Screens and values | Chosen |
|---|---|---|
| Body text | game-classic .explain 15.5px vs result-classic/timed/night .mc-exp 15px | 15.5 |
| Small mono sub-line | game-classic stub row 12px vs browse-c .sub 12.5px | 12 |
| Inline mono link | game-classic .source 13.5px vs result .why 13px | 13.5 |
| Back arrow stroke | game-classic X 2.4 and mode-select back arrow 2.4 vs browse-c Back pill arrow 2.2 | 2.4 |
| Field value | game-classic .meta dd Mono 600 15 vs browse-c pass .val Sans 800 16/1.2 (deck code Mono 600 16) | Reference on the ticket; the pass keeps its own role (field-value-pass) as a separate component |
| Field grid | game-classic: columns 1.1/1/1fr, cell padding 8/7, dd margin 2. browse-c pass: 1/1.35/0.8fr, 9/11, margin 3 | Reference for the ticket; pass documented separately |
| Carrier band | game-classic: 44px, title 16, label 12, padding 16, gap 10. browse-c pass: 30px, 14, 11, padding 14, gap 8 | Reference; compact variant for the pass |
| Stamp size | game-classic 24 vs game-timed stub stamp 28 vs result-timed New best 22 | 24 as base; others documented as variants |
| Waypoint size | game-classic and result-classic r7, square 13 vs game-streak dots and result-timed r6, 11 vs game-lives r2.6, 9 | r7/13; smaller only for density |
| Lower cloud position | top 620 in game, mode and result screens vs 660 in browse-c | 620 |
| Titles (no reference value) | mode-select 24 vs browse-c step title 22 | Both kept as screen-title and step-title; open question |
| 48px pill labels (no reference value) | result .quiet 16 vs browse-c .back 15 | Both kept |
| Shadow and on-accent tokens | Exist only in the night :root (--on-accent, --shadow-sm, --shadow-btn, --shadow-press); day screens hard-code the same literals | Tokenised for both themes with the day literals, so nothing changes visually |
| browse-c motion | browse-result.json builder note: logo leaves in 160ms, pass arrives at 100ms. File: 110ms and 120ms | File values |
| Timed hold | game-timed code holds 1000ms from the tap; builder's note suggested 700ms | 1000 (file); open question |
| Card exit direction | game-classic stub tears by result: left if correct, right if wrong. game-timed sends the card toward the answered side | Both documented; open question |
| Data, not design | browse-c sections CON 45 / SEC 47 / TEC 88 / BIL 34. mode-select shows SEC as 64 cards; the earlier reviewer standard was 52/64/70/28 | Listed only |
system.openQuestions:
1. Day contrast failures. Both need the client's sign-off, because each fix changes an approved screen.
   - The browse-c tagline uses --ink-muted on --sky-1 at 3.78:1, and 4.36:1 where it crosses into sky-2. 17px at weight 600 is not large text, so it fails WCAG 1.4.3.
   - The --accent focus ring on the True, False and ink pills reaches only 1.56 to 1.61:1 against sky-3/sky-4 in day. It fails the 3:1 required for focus and non-text contrast. Night is about 7:1.
   - Possible fixes: make the tagline --ink, and use an --ink ring on pills in day.

2. Night values that no approved screen shows:
   - The scrim: proposed rgba(0,0,0,.40).
   - The sheet shadow: derived from the night ticket recipe.
   - The whole start flow, since browse-c exists only in day.

3. Unify or keep the two title sizes: screen-title 24 (mode-select) and step-title 22 (browse-c). The same question applies to the 48px pill labels: 16 on the quiet button, 15 on Back.

4. Native safe areas: use the system insets alone, or the insets with the mock's 52/34 padding as a minimum?

5. Timed hold: the product timing is 1000ms (current file) or 700ms (builder's suggestion).

6. Tear direction: should the stub fall the way the player swiped (as Timed does) instead of by result? In the reference, a correct answer falls left and a wrong one falls right.

7. Destinations not yet designed: what follows a tap on a section row in the sheet, and where the close button on result screens leads (assumed home).

8. Web keyboard answering: the research suggests arrow keys or T/F, but no approved screen implements it, so it is not specified.

9. Content data: section card counts for CLF disagree between browse-c and mode-select. Pick one source of truth.

Facts the implementers must know:
- Weight trap: .explain and .mc-exp p set no weight. Only Overpass 600/800 are loaded, so the web renders them in SemiBold 600. Natives must request 600 explicitly.
- Licence check: Overpass and Overpass Mono are shipped as OFL 1.1 on Google Fonts. Verify the LICENSE of the exact static files bundled: SemiBold and ExtraBold, Mono Regular and SemiBold.
- Out of scope: game-streak-record.html, game-lives-out.html and game-timed-up.html appeared in the screens folder during this run, created by another worker. They are not in the approved list, so I did not read or include them.

screens.notes: I drove the whole flow in Playwright with frames at 120 ms, 250 ms and settled. Paths covered: Cloud > AWS > CLF > SEC > Classic > Start, then back one step at a time; Frontend > Next.js > Rendering > Whole deck, then back and a jump to Area through the pass; Google Cloud > CDL, which skips the section step and whose Back goes from Class to Deck; the DevOps and Azure cards, which do nothing; the continue line; first run (#first-run). No console errors and no horizontal overflow. Fixes: (1) The first choice did not travel into the pass. The step 1 to 2 move only cross-faded, but in browse-c 'Cloud' flies into Area, so that move now plays on the first step too (the 120 ms frame shows the name in flight). (2) The ready pass showed 'Best None' to first-timers and repeated the best already shown on the class card. Its middle field is now 'Cards 47', as on the approved mode-select ticket, and the unused 4th BEST entries are gone. (3) The class card's 'not yet' now reads 'not played', the approved mode-select wording. Fresh shots start-1..7. Known leftovers: in the 120 ms frames a travelling name briefly crosses the faint incoming step title (for example 'Google Cloud' over 'Choose a deck'). Twice under my paused-animation harness a step title stayed hidden (once on step 1 after Back, once on step 6 after Continue, where focus fell to body). The same click sequences replayed at real speed show the title and focus it, so I count it as a harness artifact, not a screen bug.

Same three fixes as start.html, applied to the same lines (the files differ only in tokens and on-accent glyph colours). Driven through the same full flow with no errors or overflow. Tokens match game-classic-night plus --press. Fresh shots start-night-1..7, read.

Calm and clear. The stub stays on, the statement and 'Gate Closed' turn ink-muted, an ink 'Time is up' stamp with a clock sits on the barcode, the line under it reads 'This card doesn't count · 17 answered', and the only action is 'See results →'. I briefly cut the stamp to 24px, then put it back to 28px with padding 8 18 6 so it matches the approved game-timed stub stamp (.tstamp) exactly. Net change: none. Fresh shot read.

Same as game-streak except 'New best' with a star (24px, correct green) takes the place of Correct, the old best keeps its ring on the path, and the label reads 'Previous best 12'. Screen readers still hear 'Correct.'. No changes. Fresh shots read.
Quiet ending: the third heart is struck through as the Not quite stamp lands, the label reads 'No lives left · 21 answered', and the button says 'See results →'. No changes. Fresh shots read.
Same structure as result-classic: 'Ended · 14 cards', 'Correct in a row 13', the 22px New best stamp over 'Previous best 12', and the missed list with Why. No changes. Fresh shots read.

The score said 'Cards answered' over '21 cards', saying cards twice. The label is now 'Your score', the same label result-classic uses. Everything else matches the approved results: 'Out of lives', Class / Correct / Missed, 'Equals your best', the Why disclosure. Fresh shots read.

review.remaining:
What an implementer would still have to guess:
